author: praasz
title: iGPU func tests fail en masse - no supported GPU devices found on runner
signature: Check '!m_device_map.empty()' failed: [GPU] Can't get <PROPERTY> property as no supported devices found or an error happened during devices query|Infrastructure

failed_jobs.name: iGPU Tests (func) / GPU
failed_jobs.symptom: 32927/43254 GPU func tests failed immediately with 'no supported devices found' before any test body executed

failed_jobs.name: ci/gha_overall_status
failed_jobs.symptom: Aggregate status check fails because the iGPU func test job failed

key_errors:
C++ exception with description "Exception from src/inference/src/cpp/core.cpp:272:
Exception from src/inference/src/dev/plugin.cpp:112:
Check '!m_device_map.empty()' failed at src/plugins/intel_gpu/src/plugin/plugin.cpp:593:
[GPU] Can't get DEVICE_TYPE property as no supported devices found or an error happened during devices query.
[GPU] Please check OpenVINO documentation for GPU drivers setup guide." thrown in the test body.
root_cause: The OpenCL runtime on the iGPU self-hosted runner reports 'Number of platforms 0' before any test runs, meaning the runner's GPU driver/OpenCL ICD stack did not expose any compute devices at job start. Every GPU-dependent test in the ov_gpu_func_tests binary therefore fails identically at plugin construction time ('!m_device_map.empty()' check), well before reaching any test-specific logic. The triggering commit (#39025, a CMake guard ensuring all .cl kernel source files are registered in the build) does not touch runtime device enumeration or driver setup, and the failure pattern (whole-suite day-one failure, zero platforms detected) is identical to two prior occurrences recorded for this same runner pool, confirming this is a runner/environment infrastructure problem rather than a code regression introduced by this push.
reproduction_steps: Not reproducible from the commit diff alone. To reproduce/diagnose on the runner: SSH into the iGPU runner and run `clinfo` or check `Number of platforms` via the OpenVINO GPU plugin's platform query; if it reports 0 platforms, the Intel GPU driver/OpenCL runtime (NEO compute-runtime) is not loaded, the GPU device node is inaccessible (permissions/udev rules), or the runner's GPU hardware/driver is temporarily unavailable (e.g., after a reboot or driver update).
recommended_actions: Check the iGPU self-hosted runner's GPU driver and OpenCL ICD installation (NEO compute-runtime) for the job that produced run 39472332829; restart/re-provision the runner if the device node (/dev/dri) is missing or inaccessible

Add a pre-flight smoke check step in job_gpu_tests.yml that runs a lightweight 'Number of platforms > 0' assertion before the full func-test suite, failing fast with a clear infra message instead of burning through 43k tests
Escalate to the CI infrastructure team: this is the 3rd occurrence of this exact signature on the iGPU pool within ~10 hours; consider a runner health-check/auto-recovery job
Do not block or revert PR #39025 - its diff is unrelated to GPU device enumeration
prevention_strategies: Add automated runner health monitoring that periodically verifies OpenCL device enumeration on iGPU runners and removes/re-provisions unhealthy runners from the pool before they pick up jobs. Add a fast pre-test 'platform count' gate in the GPU test job so the failure surfaces in seconds instead of after running (and failing) the full 43k-test suite.
historical_context: Identical signature recorded twice previously in pattern a5c3320815892838 (runs 39387885502 on 2026-10-20T09:11:02Z and 39398307308 on 2026-10-20T10:26:11Z), both also 'Number of platforms 0' / '!m_device_map.empty()' failures on the iGPU func test job. This is now the 3rd occurrence in roughly 10 hours, indicating a persistent or recurring runner-pool health issue rather than an isolated incident.
